model_annotations.Bulgarian: This bar chart illustrates the relationship between sparsity rate and perplexity for two different metrics, “Per-Output” and “Per-Layer”. The horizontal axis represents sparsity rate, labeled in increments from 10% to 80%, and is a categorical axis. The vertical axis represents perplexity, labeled with a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 10³ with tick labels at 10⁰, 10¹, 10², and 10³. Two sets of bars are presented for each sparsity rate: a blue bar representing “Per-Output” and an orange bar representing “Per-Layer”. For a sparsity rate of 10%, the “Per-Output” bar is approximately 3, while the “Per-Layer” bar is approximately 2. As the sparsity rate increases, both bar heights generally increase; at 80% sparsity, the “Per-Output” bar reaches approximately 950 and the “Per-Layer” bar reaches approximately 1000. The bars are arranged in ascending order based on sparsity rate, and no bars are visually emphasized with shading, bolding, outlining, or annotations.
